data.title: bn-3k8: Add runtime visual sequences and review boards

data.body: P1 memory-safety: preflight bounds only one zoomed GIF frame, while animated_gif repeatedly allocates that frame and appends every compressed frame to an uncapped Vec. A valid sequence with 240 full-screen samples at zoom 16 passes native_bytes (~59 MB) and per-frame rgba_len (~62.9 MB), yet asks the encoder to process ~15.1 GB of zoomed RGBA and permits a multi-gigabyte output allocation. This can OOM the playtest despite the documented bounded-allocation guarantee. Bound the aggregate GIF work/output (or reduce the accepted sample/zoom product), enforce the limit before stepping, and add a regression showing this maximum-shaped request is rejected.

data.reason: Request changes: GIF preflight does not bound aggregate encoding work or output, so accepted 240-frame/high-zoom scenarios can exhaust memory despite the bounded-visual-allocation contract. Exact cadence/crop, deterministic artifacts, v1 compatibility, and native reference labeling otherwise passed focused review.

data.body: Fixed in 15586a4: preflight now rejects aggregate zoomed GIF RGBA work above 64 MiB before stepping, and animated_gif enforces the same bound defensively. Added a maximum-shaped 240-frame/full-screen/zoom-16 schema regression plus a direct encoder regression; focused tests and clippy pass.

Verified in 15586a4. The same checked aggregate RGBA calculation now runs in preflight before stepping and again at the encoder boundary; the 64 MiB aggregate cap also bounds the indexed GIF payload to a smaller finite workload. Both the maximum-shaped schema regression and direct encoder regression pass.

data.reason: Approved after 15586a4: aggregate GIF work is checked before stepping and defensively in animated_gif; maximum-shaped and direct-encoder regressions pass.
